stories.title: Add image URLs to XML sitemap for Google image indexing
stories.description: Next.js 15 sitemap.ts natively supports an `images` array on each sitemap entry, which generates the correct `xmlns:image` namespace and `<image:image>` tags required by Google's image sitemap extension. Adding hero images, room photos, and OG images to the sitemap enables Google Images indexing, which drives additional organic traffic for visual traveller queries.
acceptanceCriteria: sitemap.ts includes an `images` array for every route that has a representative image (home, rooms, gallery, blog posts)
Generated sitemap XML validates against Google's image sitemap schema (namespace xmlns:image='http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-image/1.1' present)
Google Search Console shows image sitemap entries parsed without errors after resubmission
At least the hero image URL is listed for the home route and at least the OG image URL for each blog post route
technicalNotes: Use the `images` property on each sitemap entry object: `{ url, images: [{ url: absoluteImageUrl }] }`
Next.js 15 sitemap spec: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/sitemap
Google image sitemap reference: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/sitemaps/image-sitemaps

stories.title: Implement WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 – Target Size Minimum (24×24 CSS px)
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 introduced SC 2.5.8 at Level AA, requiring all interactive targets (buttons, links, form controls) to have a hit area of at least 24×24 CSS pixels or sufficient offset spacing from adjacent targets. This directly benefits mobile users and people with motor disabilities, and is now a baseline requirement for WCAG 2.2 AA conformance.
acceptanceCriteria: All interactive elements (nav links, buttons, form controls, social icons, close buttons) have a minimum computed hit area of 24×24 CSS pixels verified via DevTools
Icon-only buttons (WhatsApp FAB, close X, share) are explicitly sized to at least 44×44 CSS px (best practice above the minimum)
Inline hyperlinks within blog post body text are exempt under the inline-text exception
Automated axe-core or Lighthouse accessibility scan reports no SC 2.5.8 violations
Manual test confirms no adjacent targets are closer than 24 CSS px without sufficient target size
technicalNotes: Apply `min-width: 24px; min-height: 24px` (or padding equivalent) via Tailwind `p-*` utilities on all button and icon-link components
The 'spacing' exception allows targets smaller than 24px if there is ≥24px offset from any adjacent target — measure carefully for nav items
W3C Understanding SC 2.5.8: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html

stories.title: Implement WCAG 2.2 SC 3.2.6 – Consistent Help placement (Level A)
stories.description: SC 3.2.6 (Level A) requires that any help mechanism present on multiple pages — such as a WhatsApp contact link, phone number, or FAQ link — appears in the same relative order in the page structure across all pages. As a hospitality website with a WhatsApp CTA in the navbar and footer, this criterion is directly applicable and needed for full WCAG 2.2 AA (which includes all Level A) compliance.
acceptanceCriteria: WhatsApp contact link, phone number, or 'Contact Us' mechanism appears in an identical DOM order relative to surrounding navigation/footer elements on every page
If a Help/FAQ link is present in the header of one page, it appears in the same header position on all pages where it exists
Audit of all page templates (home, rooms, guide, blog, contact, book) confirms consistent help mechanism placement
Accessibility statement or audit report documents conformance with SC 3.2.6
technicalNotes: This does not require adding help on every page — only that where it exists, it is in the same relative position
Shared layout components (Header, Footer) naturally satisfy this if the help element is always in those components
W3C Understanding SC 3.2.6: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/consistent-help.html

stories.title: Add prefers-reduced-motion support for all CSS/JS animations
stories.description: Users with vestibular disorders, epilepsy, or ADHD can configure their OS to request reduced motion. The `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` CSS media query should disable or drastically simplify all decorative transitions, parallax, fade-in scroll animations, and hover effects on the site. This is required for WCAG 2.3.3 (Animation from Interactions, AAA) and is widely considered a baseline accessibility best practice.
acceptanceCriteria: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` CSS block disables all non-essential transitions and animations site-wide
Scroll-triggered fade-in or slide-in animations are instant (no transition) when reduced motion is active
Any JavaScript-driven animations (e.g., counters, carousels) check `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` before animating
Testing with OS accessibility setting 'Reduce Motion' enabled shows no decorative movement
Essential motion (e.g., loading spinners) is retained but non-decorative transitions are simplified
technicalNotes: Add a global CSS rule: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; } }`
For JS animations use: `const prefersReducedMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches`
React hook approach: https://www.joshwcomeau.com/react/prefers-reduced-motion/
MDN reference: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/@media/prefers-reduced-motion

stories.title: Add Malaysia PDPA-compliant cookie consent banner with explicit opt-in
stories.description: Malaysia's Personal Data Protection (Amendment) Act 2024, effective from January 2025, requires explicit affirmative opt-in consent before setting non-essential cookies (analytics, marketing). Implied consent (continuing to browse) is invalid under the PDPA. The site currently uses analytics without a consent gate, creating legal exposure for a Malaysian-registered business.
acceptanceCriteria: Cookie consent banner appears on first visit before any analytics or non-essential cookies are set
Banner offers explicit 'Accept', 'Reject', and 'Manage Preferences' options — no pre-ticked boxes
Google Analytics / Microsoft Clarity scripts only load after user accepts analytics cookies
User preference is stored in localStorage/cookie and respected across sessions
Privacy Policy page is updated to describe cookie categories, retention periods, and third-party recipients
Banner text is available in both English and Chinese (matching existing hreflang)
technicalNotes: Use a lightweight library such as `vanilla-cookieconsent` or Next.js-compatible `react-cookie-consent`
Implement consent-based script loading: wrap GA/Clarity initialization in a consent check
Malaysia PDPA Amendment Act 2024 in force from 1 January 2025: https://www.aseanbriefing.com/news/malaysia-tightens-data-protection-from-june-2025/
Cookiebot PDPA overview: https://www.cookiebot.com/en/malaysia-pdpa/

stories.title: Add Privacy Policy page with PDPA-required disclosures
stories.description: Malaysia's PDPA requires data controllers to provide a privacy notice accessible from the website disclosing: types of personal data collected, purposes of processing, third-party disclosures, data retention periods, user rights (access, correction, withdrawal), and a contact method for data requests. The Amendment Act 2024 (Phase 3, June 2025) adds mandatory data portability disclosures. The site currently lacks a dedicated privacy policy page.
acceptanceCriteria: A /privacy-policy route exists and is accessible from the footer on every page
Privacy policy covers: data categories collected, collection purposes, third parties (Google Analytics, Resend, Sentry), retention periods, and Malaysian data subject rights
A data request contact method (email or form) is provided per PDPA requirements
Page includes a 'Last Updated' date and is written in plain language
Footer includes working links to both Privacy Policy and, if applicable, Terms of Service
technicalNotes: Required disclosures for Malaysia PDPA: https://malaysia.incorp.asia/guides/pdpa-compliance-malaysia-complete-guide/
The privacy policy must be accessible before any data collection occurs — link in header or footer is sufficient

June 2025 PDPA amendment adds data portability rights which should be documented: https://www.dfdl.com/insights/legal-and-tax-updates/malaysia-implementation-of-the-personal-data-protection-amendment-act-2024/

stories.title: Add Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy security headers
stories.description: OWASP 2025 secure headers guidance recommends `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` and `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin` to enforce cross-origin isolation, enabling access to high-resolution timers and SharedArrayBuffer while preventing cross-origin data leaks via Spectre-class side-channel attacks. These are distinct from the already-implemented `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` header.
acceptanceCriteria: `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin` header present on all page responses (verified via curl or browser DevTools)
`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` header present on HTML page responses

No third-party embeds (e.g., Google Maps iframes) break due to the COEP restriction — either they are removed, replaced with cross-origin-compatible alternatives, or COEP is set to `credentialless` if needed
SecurityHeaders.com score is A or A+ after addition
Vercel deployment headers config in next.config.ts updated
technicalNotes: COEP `require-corp` blocks subresources that don't send CORP or CORS headers — audit all third-party scripts/images first
If Google Maps or other third-party iframes are used, consider `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless` as a less strict alternative
OWASP Secure Headers Project: https://owasp.org/www-project-secure-headers/
MDN CORP: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Guides/Cross-Origin_Resource_Policy

stories.title: Add TouristTrip schema for featured Johor Bahru itineraries on /guide
stories.description: Schema.org's `TouristTrip` type (developed by the W3C Tourism Structured Web Data Community Group) describes complete tourist journeys and itineraries. Adding TouristTrip markup to the JB travel guide page for 'Day trip from Singapore' or '3-day JB itinerary' content could qualify for rich results in travel-intent queries and improve discoverability for itinerary-seeking travellers — the site's primary audience.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one TouristTrip JSON-LD block added to /guide page describing a named JB itinerary
Schema includes required properties: `name`, `description`, `itinerary` (ItemList of TouristAttraction), and `touristType`
Schema validates without errors in Google's Rich Results Test
TouristTrip `offers` property references the hostel with a price if the trip is bookable
Schema.org TouristTrip type is used (not a custom type)
technicalNotes: Schema.org TouristTrip: https://schema.org/TouristTrip
The `itinerary` property accepts a single `ItemList` of `ListItem` objects each referencing a `TouristAttraction`
The `touristType` property should use an Audience type value such as `Backpacker` or `BudgetTraveler`
W3C Tourism Structured Web Data CG: https://www.w3.org/community/tourismdata/

stories.title: Add Speakable structured data to key hostel information sections
stories.description: Google's Speakable structured data (beta) marks sections of a page as suitable for text-to-speech playback by Google Assistant. Adding `speakable` with CSS selectors pointing to the hostel name, location, check-in/check-out times, and key amenities sections enables voice search users — particularly travellers making hands-free queries — to hear the most relevant hostel information directly from a Google Assistant response.
acceptanceCriteria: A `speakable` property with `SpeakableSpecification` is added to the LodgingBusiness JSON-LD on the home page
`cssSelector` values target the hostel tagline, address block, and amenities summary (each section ≤30 seconds of audio when read aloud)
Markup validated using Google's Rich Results Test (speakable is listed as a test-supported type)
Targeted sections are written in clear, natural spoken language (no jargon, short sentences)
The JSON-LD does not reference non-existent CSS selectors — selectors are verified against the rendered DOM
technicalNotes: Google Speakable documentation: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/speakable
Each speakable section should be 20-30 seconds when read aloud (~50-75 words)
Use `cssSelector` array to target specific DOM IDs or class names rather than XPath for maintainability
Speakable is currently in beta and limited to news publishers in Google's full rollout, but the markup is accepted and processed

stories.title: Optimise contact form with React 19 useActionState and optimistic UI
stories.description: The current contact form uses a client-side fetch to a Server Action. Migrating to React 19's `useActionState` hook provides built-in pending state management, eliminating the need for manual `useState` for loading/error states. Adding `useOptimistic` for instant success feedback before the Resend API call completes improves perceived performance and reduces booking abandonment.
acceptanceCriteria: Contact form uses `useActionState` (React 19) instead of manual useState for pending/error/success states
Submit button shows a spinner and is disabled while the action is pending — driven by `useActionState`'s `isPending` value
On submission, an optimistic 'Message sent!' confirmation appears immediately via `useOptimistic`, with error recovery if the server action fails
If server action returns a validation error, field-level error messages are displayed without a full re-render
TypeScript types are correct for the action state shape
technicalNotes: React 19 `useActionState` docs: https://react.dev/reference/react/useActionState
`useFormStatus` can be used in a child `SubmitButton` component to read pending state without prop drilling
Next.js 15 forms guide: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/forms
The `useOptimistic` hook: https://react.dev/reference/react/useOptimistic

stories.title: Use next/font with variable font and size-adjust fallback for LCP improvement
stories.description: Next.js's `next/font` module automatically self-hosts Google Fonts, eliminating render-blocking external font requests. When configured with a `variable` font (a single file containing all weights), it also generates an optimal `size-adjust` CSS fallback that prevents layout shift (CLS) during font swap. The current setup likely uses static-weight Google Font imports which incur external network requests and potential CLS.
acceptanceCriteria: All Google Fonts loaded via `next/font/google` with no `<link rel='stylesheet' href='fonts.googleapis.com/...'>`  in rendered HTML
Font declarations use the `variable` option (e.g., `subsets: ['latin']`, `variable: '--font-inter'`) to load a single variable font file
No external fonts.googleapis.com or fonts.gstatic.com network requests visible in DevTools Network panel
CLS score in Lighthouse ≤ 0.1 with font loaded for the first time (cold cache)
Font CSS custom property (`--font-inter`) is referenced in Tailwind config fontFamily
technicalNotes: Next.js font optimization docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fonts
Variable fonts reduce HTTP requests: one file for all weights vs. separate files per weight
next/font generates `size-adjust` automatically for the fallback font to prevent CLS
Self-hosted fonts also improve privacy (no Google tracking requests from user browsers)

stories.title: Add Referrer-Policy and X-Content-Type-Options security headers
stories.description: OWASP Secure Headers Project identifies `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` as required baseline security headers. `X-Content-Type-Options` prevents MIME-sniffing attacks and `Referrer-Policy` controls what URL information is sent to third-party analytics endpoints. Both are absent from the current `next.config.ts` headers configuration based on the existing security header inventory.
acceptanceCriteria: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` header present on all responses (HTML, JS, CSS, images)
`Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` header present on all HTML page responses
SecurityHeaders.com scan reports A or A+ rating after addition
curl -I on production URL shows both headers present
No existing functionality broken — analytics still receives origin information for same-origin navigations
technicalNotes: Add both to the `headers()` array in next.config.ts under the `source: '/(.*)'` pattern
`strict-origin-when-cross-origin` sends full URL for same-origin, only origin for cross-origin, nothing for downgrade (HTTPS→HTTP)
OWASP HTTP Security Headers Cheat Sheet: https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/HTTP_Headers_Cheat_Sheet.html
`X-Content-Type-Options` should apply to all routes including API routes and static assets

stories.title: Register Google Business Profile and connect to Google Hotel free booking links
stories.description: Google Hotel free booking links allow accommodation properties to appear in Google Search hotel results at zero cost per click. This requires a verified Google Business Profile linked to the property and a connectivity partner (or the new direct rate-sharing beta) to send real-time availability. For a hostel without an OTA manager, this is the highest-ROI distribution channel improvement available.
acceptanceCriteria: Google Business Profile for Pelangi Capsule Hostel is claimed and fully verified with correct name, address, phone, and website URL
Business Profile shows live reviews, photos, amenities, and correct check-in/check-out hours
Property is connected to Google Hotel Center via a connectivity partner (e.g., Cloudbeds, Beds24) or the direct Google rate-sharing feature
Free booking links appear in Google Search for the property name query pointing to the direct booking page
Booking landing page URL matches the property's own domain (not an OTA link)
technicalNotes: Google Hotel free booking links getting started: https://travel.google/partners/hotels/get-started/
Free booking links have zero cost-per-click unlike Hotel Ads
Beds24, Cloudbeds, and Little Hotelier are connectivity partners that support small properties without full PMS
The booking landing page must be on the property's own domain — the existing /book page qualifies

stories.title: Implement INP optimisation: defer non-critical third-party scripts
stories.description: Interaction to Next Paint (INP) replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024. The primary INP threat on this site is third-party script main-thread contention — analytics, chat widgets, and tracking scripts that execute synchronously during user interactions. Using `next/script` with `strategy='lazyOnload'` for non-critical scripts and the Scheduler API (`scheduler.postTask`) for deferred work improves INP below the 200ms 'good' threshold.
acceptanceCriteria: All non-critical third-party scripts (analytics, Clarity, chat) use `<Script strategy='lazyOnload'>` via next/script
INP measured by web-vitals v4 in the field is ≤ 200ms (good) for P75 across Chrome UX Report
No long tasks (>50ms) attributable to third-party scripts visible in Lighthouse 'Avoid long main-thread tasks' audit
Lighthouse Performance score does not regress after script deferral
web-vitals attribution data logged to analytics identifies the specific interaction with highest INP
technicalNotes: Next.js Script strategies: `beforeInteractive` (critical), `afterInteractive` (default), `lazyOnload` (lowest priority), `worker` (Partytown)
web.dev INP optimization guide: https://web.dev/articles/optimize-inp
Use Chrome DevTools Performance panel to identify long tasks triggered by interactions
The Scheduler API (`scheduler.postTask`) enables yield-based task chunking for long event handlers: https://web.dev/articles/scheduler-yield

stories.title: Add accessibility statement page documenting WCAG 2.2 AA conformance
stories.description: An accessibility statement is the recommended way to document a site's WCAG conformance level, known limitations, and contact method for users who experience barriers. While not legally mandated for private Malaysian businesses under PDPA, it is a best practice recommended by W3C WAI and is increasingly expected by international travellers — especially those from the EU or UK where accessibility statements are legally required for public sector and many private sites.
acceptanceCriteria: An /accessibility route exists and is linked from the site footer
Page states the conformance target (WCAG 2.2 Level AA) and date of last assessment
Page lists any known non-conformances with brief descriptions and planned remediation timelines
A contact method (email) is provided for users to report accessibility barriers
Page is written in plain English and does not itself have accessibility issues
technicalNotes: W3C WAI accessibility statement generator: https://www.w3.org/WAI/planning/statements/
Template includes sections: conformance status, technical specifications, known limitations, feedback contact
The statement should be updated whenever a significant accessibility audit is performed
Linking from footer ensures consistent help mechanism (SC 3.2.6 compliance for the contact method)
